public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1159

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1159](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1159)
- [ESS83] Erdős, P. and Silverman, R. and Stein, A., *Intersection properties of families containing
  sets of nearly the same size*. Ars Combin. (1983), 247--259.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Configuration

namespace Erdos1159

/--
Determine whether there exists a constant $C>1$ such that the following holds.

Let $P$ be a finite [projective plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projective_plane). Must there exist a set of points $S$ such that $1\leq \lvert S\cap \ell\rvert \leq C$ for all lines $\ell$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_1159 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C : ℕ, 1 < C ∧
      ∀ (P L : Type) (_ : Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L),
        ∀ _ : ProjectivePlane P L, ∃ S : Set P, ∀ l : L,
          1 ≤ (S ∩ {p : P | p ∈ l}).ncard ∧ (S ∩ {p : P | p ∈ l}).ncard ≤ C := by
  sorry

end Erdos1159

reformulations.difference: Lean chooses the uniform absolute bound C in ℕ rather than allowing a real bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any real bound C > 1 can be increased to a natural number N ≥ C, preserving every intersection bound and 1 < N. Conversely, a natural bound gives a real bound by casting. The equivalence, retaining all the finite-projective-plane quantifiers, was proved as natBound_iff_realBound in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Erdős, On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved (1981), block-design question 1: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf

Erdős–Silverman–Stein, Intersection properties of families containing sets of nearly the same size (1983), abstract, introduction and projective-plane results: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1983-07.pdf
Ben Green, 100 Open Problems, remarks following Problem 68: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf
Mathlib/Combinatorics/Configuration.lean: Nondegenerate, HasPoints, HasLines, ProjectivePlane and finite-plane cardinality lemmas
Mathlib/Data/Set/Card.lean: Set.ncard and its finite-set interpretation
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the uniform bounded-blocking-set question in Erdős's 1981 paper. The source site's OPEN status agrees with the category. Checked quantifier scope, incidence axioms, finiteness and cardinality semantics. Successful Lean checks exclude empty/undersized planes, establish that all counted intersections are finite, and construct a seven-point Fano plane satisfying the hypotheses. Exhaustive small-case tests find no admissible set for C ≤ 2 and admissible sets for C = 3, as expected. Direct site access was challenged; its status and remarks were read through the reader endpoint and the exact mathematical question was verified in the primary papers.
